text:
raj_customer: Hey @support — customers reporting a bunch of requests routing to EU with ~200ms extra latency and unexpected EU billing. This started ~15:12 UTC. We send a region preference in a header but looks ignored. Sample request headers below and request-id: req_0a1b2c3d

raj_customer: curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***" -H "X-Region-Preference: us-west||eu" \n  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hi"}'

maya_support: Thanks @raj_customer — sorry about this. Can you paste one full raw request + response headers (including any X-Edge-Region or x-request-id) and a couple of request-ids/times so we can look in router logs? Also is this reproducible from your CI?

raj_customer: Pasting one example: request-id: req_0a1b2c3d, timestamp 2025-06-04T15:12:41Z
  Request headers:
  Host: api.redwood.example
  Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***
  X-Region-Preference: us-west||eu
  User-Agent: acme-sdk/2.3.1
  Response headers seen by client:
  x-request-id: req_0a1b2c3d
  X-Edge-Region: eu-west-1
  via: edge-12

  Repro: Yes we can repro from CI with same header string. We tried variants: single pipe works, double-pipe causes EU routing.

maya_support: Got it. Tagging infra/eng routing. @lina_engineer can you check routing parse for pipe-delimited header precedence? Adding logs: req_0a1b2c3d

lina_engineer: Looking. I pulled router trace for req_0a1b2c3d — router receives header value exactly "us-west||eu". The parser does split on /[|,;\s]/ and then applies trimming, but we have a bug where empty tokens (result of consecutive delimiters) are kept and treated as the highest-priority token (empty -> fallback-> maps to default-region=eu because empty token triggers legacy fallback). Repro snippet from our trace: split('us-west||eu') -> ["us-west", "", "eu"] -> filter step missing -> precedence picks first non-null-ish -> empty considered higher than eu in our precedence comparator.

lina_engineer: Quick root cause: recent change to unify multi-delimiter support removed the filter that dropped zero-length entries. This only affects pipe as a delimiter because other SDKs mostly send commas.

lina_engineer: Workaround options:
  1) Temporary router rule (hotfix): drop zero-length tokens before precedence evaluation. I can push this as a config rollout.
  2) Client-side: trim out empty tokens in header (ACME SDK 2.3.2 will fix this).
  3) Long-term: update router parsing to canonicalize header entries and log telemetry when empty tokens seen.

lina_engineer: Example admin API call to add temporary rule (internal only):
  POST /admin/routing/rules
  Body:
  {
    "match": {"header": "X-Region-Preference"},
    "action": "filter_empty_tokens",
    "delimiter": "|"
  }

maya_support: @lina_engineer please apply option 1 as a temporary mitigation. Also filing an incident for tracking. @billing_bot can we proactively credit the EU overage while this is investigated?

billing_bot: Filed billing ticket BT-9832. We'll issue a provisional credit for measured EU charges from 15:10-15:40 UTC once eng confirms mitigation.

deploy-bot: route-rule-deploy job started (job_id: rr-7712)

deploy-bot: route-rule-deploy succeeded (job_id: rr-7712) — rule: filter_empty_tokens applied to X-Region-Preference

lina_engineer: Confirming after rollout: new router behavior drops empty tokens before precedence; I retried the CI repro and now requests with "us-west||eu" route to us-west as expected. Logs: req_0a1b2c3d now shows X-Edge-Region: us-west-2.

maya_support: @raj_customer can you re-run your CI check (or give me a sample request time) so we can confirm on your side? We've applied temporary rule and engaged SDK team for 2.3.2 patch.

raj_customer: Re-ran CI at 2025-06-04T15:25:03Z — looks good, routing to us-west now. Latency back to baseline. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

maya_support: Great — closing the support thread when billing confirms credit. Follow-ups: eng will ship permanent fix in next router release and SDK team will push 2.3.2 to strip empty tokens.

maya_support: Action items:
  - lina_engineer: ship permanent router fix (tracking INC-4721)
  - sdk-team: release 2.3.2 to sanitize region header values
  - billing_bot: confirm credit completed and message customer

billing_bot: Credit applied (BT-9832) — customer credited for EU overages between 15:10-15:40 UTC.

maya_support: Thanks everyone, marking resolved from support side. :white_check_mark:
